articles.title: Lynxes Caught Soaking Their Prey—A Carnivore First That Hints at Hidden Smarts
articles.summary: In a world first, Iberian lynxes have been recorded dunking dead rabbits in water. Five females in central Spain repeatedly soaked prey, possibly to hydrate cubs or soften meat. The behavior spread among related cats, suggesting social learning in a species once nearly extinct.

articles.title: A Knotted Fiber That Leaps Like a Bug—And Could Help Reforest the Planet
articles.summary: Engineers have built a soft, millimeter-thick fiber that, when heated, explosively unties itself and jumps nearly 2 meters high. The knot stores elastic energy, mimicking a springtail's leap. By tweaking knot topology and adding wings, researchers control its flight—opening doors for agricultural and reforestation robots.

articles.title: AI in Health Care: Why the Best Algorithms Need a Doctor's Touch
articles.summary: AI is flooding into medicine—over 1,300 FDA-approved devices now interpret scans, plan surgeries, and streamline workflows. But health care's complexity demands deep collaboration between developers and clinicians to avoid failures. Tailored solutions that reduce caregiver burden are the priority, yet immature AI remains a top adoption barrier.
